summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of Giovanni Pisano, a sculptor born in Pisa and trained in the workshop of his father, the sculptor Nicola Pisano. It covers his early collaborations with his father on the Siena Cathedral pulpit and the Fontana Maggiore in Perugia, and his move to Siena. It also notes that his early work is hard to separate from his father's, while his Madonna with Child can be attributed to him with certainty.
one_line: Biography of Giovanni Pisano, Pisan sculptor and son of Nicola Pisano, his collaborations with his father, and his early independent work.
key_facts: Giovanni Pisano was born in Pisa.
Giovanni Pisano was the son of the famous sculptor Nicola Pisano.
Giovanni Pisano received his training in the workshop of his father, Nicola Pisano.
In 1265–1268, Giovanni Pisano worked with his father on the pulpit in Siena Cathedral.
The fountain "Fontana Maggiore" in Perugia was his next major work with his father, completed in 1278.
Nicola Pisano is thought to have died either around 1278 or in 1284.
Giovanni Pisano took up residence in Siena in 1284 (per the note's alternative dating, when Nicola is thought to have died).
His first works were made in Nicola's style, and it is difficult to separate the contributions of the two artists.
The "Madonna with Child" can be attributed with certainty to Giovanni Pisano.
The "Madonna with Child" shows a new style with a certain familiarity between Mother and Child.
